open_requirements.requirement: Discord bot with rec commands, per-fandom feeds, account linking
open_requirements.notes: Gaps review E5. Extends §37 companion bot. | UNBLOCKED 2026-11-11 (credential supplied; token stored on the host only, never in the tree — [REDACTED] here). SCOPE DECISION: the spec's separate workspace with Poise+Serenity+Redis is rejected for this deployment — no Redis in the stack, a gateway websocket is a new always-on failure mode, and a separate workspace is invisible to gate.sh. It ships as an INTERACTIONS ENDPOINT on the existing server (Discord POSTs signed interactions; Ed25519 verified BEFORE parsing), so dispatch is an Axum handler the existing gates cover. Seven steps with acceptance tests are in docs/plans/roadmap-remaining.md; step 2 (signature before parse) and the /users/@me live proof come first. | CENSUS 2026-11-11 superseded my own plan: a darkhold bot ALREADY EXISTS (code-local/rust/darkbot, 12.5k lines, darkbot-adapter trait + conformance suite + discord/matrix/telegram). The interactions endpoint I wrote this turn was deleted — it was the third hand-rolled copy (ascend 818, darkhold 223, suki 170) of a ~120-line kit (leverage 9 = 3x3/1: not worth a crate). darkbot already calls darkhold's real API (public/search, public/works, works/{}/kudos, me/tokens, me/tokens/{}) which all exist. Its link handshake (bot/link/start + bot/link/exchange) contradicts §23.2, which is implemented and better: /me/bots/{id}/link-challenge -> GET /bots/link/{code} (reader sees what is asked) -> POST /bots/link/{code} (confirm; token issued once to the reader's session). darkbot adapts, not the server. REMAINING: point darkbot at live darkhold, adapt its two link calls, prove one command in a real guild. The shareable component is darkbot-adapter's PlatformMessage IR + Adapter trait + conformance (the second implementation is fanfic-archivist-bot's archivist-core, 30.7k lines) — converge only when a second non-darkhold bot needs it. | LINK CARDINALITY FIXED 2026-11-11 (M45-59): §23.2's confirmation used to rotate the registration's credential, making the bot single-reader — the second person to link revoked the first one's token and bot_for_token could not see links at all. Links are now per (bot, pseud) and suspension reaches them. REMAINING on this row is the credential half only: (1) a Discord APPLICATION for darkhold (the host holds only ~/.config/ascend-bot.env, which is ascend's identity — reusing it would post darkbot's replies as ascend), its token in ~/.config/darkbot-bot.env 0600, never in the tree; (2) DARKBOT_DARKHOLD_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8081/api/v1 plus DARKBOT_STORE_KEY (32 bytes hex); (3) the bot invited to a guild and one command proved live; (4) darkbot's two invented calls (bot/link/start, bot/link/exchange) replaced by GET /bots/link/{code} describe + the reader-confirms-on-the-site model. | CENSUS 2026-11-12 (step 4, the code half, measured before writing any): the two calls darkbot invents cannot simply be redirected, because darkhold's §23.2 flow is OWNER-INITIATED, not bot-initiated. `POST /me/bots/{id}/link-challenge` takes `RequireSession` — the bot's OWNER mints a code in a browser — and `GET/POST /bots/link/{code}` is the reader confirming on the site. That works for 'my bot, my account' and cannot work for a guild bot that must start the flow FOR a reader inside Discord: the bot has a bearer credential, not a session, so it cannot mint a code at all. That asymmetry is the reason darkbot grew `bot/link/start` + `bot/link/exchange`. THE SLICE THIS NEEDS (designed here, not yet built): (1) accept a BEARER bot credential on the challenge door, resolved through the existing `external::bot_for_token` + suspension check, with the bot id taken from the token rather than the path; (2) carry the platform identity (`platform`, `platform_user_id`) on the challenge row so a code is bound to the person it was minted for, and copy it onto the link row at confirmation — without it the bot cannot tell which Discord user a link belongs to, which is the entire question it is asking; (3) `GET /me/bots/{id}/links` (bearer) returning per-pseud links and their platform users, so the bot learns the outcome; (4) the reader still confirms on the site — the bot must never be able to confirm its own challenge, or 'what am I granting' becomes a page nobody reads. REMAINING BLOCKER beyond code: a Discord APPLICATION for darkhold itself (the host holds only ascend's identity; reusing it posts darkbot's replies as ascend) and a guild invite. Credential half only. | CODE HALF BUILT 2026-11-12 (step 4; the row still needs the credential): any bot credential now mints a challenge for a named platform user and reads back who linked. CENSUS: ADAPT — the three §23.2 doors existed, the principal did not. A bot registration's token carries acting_pseud_id NULL (0083), so RequireActor answered 403 at the mint door and resolve_bearer answered 401 before the handler could 404 a suspended bot; auth::BotCaller::{Session,Bot} + RequireBotOrOwner name the two callers instead of flattening them into one Actor, and bot_registration_for_token matches the registration's OWN token_id (not a linked reader's) and returns its state so the handler answers 404. Migration 0215 (both dialects) puts platform + platform_user_id on link_challenges; the reader still confirms on the site (a bot that could confirm its own challenge makes 'what am I granting' a page nobody reads); GET /me/bots/{id}/links returns per-pseud links with platform, platform_user, linked_at, and bot_name from api_tokens.name (bot_registrations has no name column). PostgreSQL needed ::text casts on both sides of uuid = text joins (api_tokens.id is UUID, token_id is TEXT). CREDENTIAL+GATEWAY 2026-11-19: supplied Discord application stored out-of-tree 0600, verified via Discord API; darkbot gateway wired with Bot auth header, shared on_payload parser, heartbeat, reconnect and opt-in MESSAGE_CONTENT; live run reached READY. Remaining: enable MESSAGE_CONTENT in the developer portal and invite the bot to a guild for one real command.

open_requirements.requirement: dh audit --since 7d: the account owner sees every write their tokens made
open_requirements.notes: Power-user sweep P25. Automation is accountable to the person it acts for; the operation log already records the writes. | HALF-BUILT 2026-11-11 (server side done, verb not written, attribution impossible as the schema stands). SHIPPED: `GET /api/v1/me/audit-log` now takes `since` (RFC 3339) and `limit` (1..200, default 50) and echoes both back. Without a lower bound the route could only answer 'the newest fifty entries', which is not the question: a quiet account's week falls off the end of the page and a busy one's page covers an hour. The bound is NORMALISED to second precision with `identity::format_rfc3339` before it reaches SQL, because this schema stores `created_at` at second precision on purpose and a caller's `.500` fraction compares digit-by-digit back to front — so a fraction would silently exclude the entry it names. A bound that is not a timestamp is refused 422 naming the format it wants, rather than ignored, because ignoring it answers a different question than the one asked. TESTS: milestone_14 my_audit_log_takes_a_lower_bound_and_normalises_a_fraction_to_the_column 1/1 SQLite and 1/1 PostgreSQL — three entries at 2026-11-01/05/10, `since=11-05T00:00:00Z` returns [new, middle] and includes its own instant, `since=11-05T00:00:00.500Z` returns the same two and echoes `2026-11-05T00:00:00Z`, `limit=1` returns the newest, `since=7d` is 422. MUTANT: the comparison flipped to `<=` -> the list comes back as [middle, old]. MISSING, and why the row stays planned: (1) `dh audit --since 7d` — the CLI verb, which must resolve relative durations client-side and send RFC 3339 (deliberately not implemented yet, so the row is not claimed); (2) ATTRIBUTION: `audit_log` has no token id column, so the row's own words — 'every write their tokens made' — cannot be answered. `list_audit_log` scopes by `actor`, which is the human. Telling a reader 'your token did this' needs the write path to record which credential was used; until it does, the honest surface is 'what your account did', and the row's claim is only half met. CLI WINDOW SHIPPED 2026-11-19: dh audit --since 7d resolves relative durations client-side; fake-origin test 1/1, mutant red/restored. Still blocked: audit_log has no token id, so per-token attribution is still unavailable.

open_requirements.requirement: fandom tags cover the whole catalogue and can be ranked: backfill tags for the sb/sv/qq/ao3/ffnet estate and import the endorsement counts the tagged rows lack
open_requirements.notes: Found while shipping M63-01. The filter works and is honest about coverage (fandom_tagged_rows / fandom_tagged_with_likes), but as data it answers 'Naruto' with 265 pawchive rows that carry no likes, so --sort likes orders ties. The tagging came in with the pawchive importer; the forum and AO3 imports wrote no tags. Needs either a backfill from the source metadata (AO3 tags are in the work page the importer already fetches) or a tag-inference pass, and a like-count import for pawchive. b387cb1e: the inference route is built — db::tag_inference::propose_from_text matches existing tag nodes against stored title/summary text and writes Claimant::Model proposals (inferred+unconfirmed ⇒ invisible to readers), longest node wins and a subsumed shorter node is dropped; db::tag_inference::coverage reports per source items/tagged/with_likes/tagged_and_liked with tagged counting only reader-visible rows. Operator doors GET /operator/tag-inference/coverage and POST /operator/tag-inference/run?limit= (1..5000). NOT DONE and not doable here: the importer stores no category field (0006_imports.sql), so a metadata backfill needs re-fetching source pages — that is the remaining half, plus pawchive's like-count import.

open_requirements.requirement: one shared taste crate and one JSON schema set, so darkhold and suki compute blend, affinity and the passport identically
open_requirements.notes: The synergy row, and the one that keeps the others honest: two products that each implement the blend will disagree within a month, and a passport whose semantics differ between sender and receiver is worse than none. A small Rust crate with no product dependencies plus versioned JSON schemas; both binaries depend on it, neither forks it. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.  | CENSUS 2026-11-11 (measured, no code written): REUSE the mechanism, BUILD the crate. (1) No shared taste crate exists: `ls ~/code-local/rust` has polaris-candidates and polaris-eval, no polaris-taste. (2) The duplication is real and counted: `rg -l -i 'fn blend|affinity'` over the estate gives darkhold 55 files, suki 38, ascend 7, whitebois 4, tessera 4, orbitals 4, commons 1. (3) darkhold already HAS a taste crate (crates/taste, 'the taste engine: the catalogue, the graph, the ranker and the budgets', binaries + lib) but it depends on `darkhold-domain` — so it cannot be the shared crate as it stands: extracting it means deciding which types move out of the product's domain first. That is the real work of this row, and it is a design decision, not a copy. (4) The estate ALREADY has the shared-crate pattern and uses it here: crates/taste depends on `polaris-eval` by relative path '../../../../polaris-eval', with a comment saying 'path dependency until the Forgejo registry answers' — so the publishing mechanism the row asks for is REUSE, and its precondition (a registry that answers) is the one thing this row does not control. DECISION (recorded, not yet implemented): the shared crate is `polaris-taste`, containing the pure parts of darkhold-taste that speak only in domain primitives (budget, diversify, ladder, embed) plus the affinity/blend math, with the product-shaped parts (catalogue, graph, collab, health — which read a table or a product's rows) staying in each product behind a trait the shared crate defines. The JSON schema set is versioned with the crate, and the passport schema is the one that must be identical on both sides because a passport whose semantics differ between sender and receiver is worse than none. NOT STARTED: no crate was created, because a crate nothing depends on is the 'component nobody calls' failure, and the first commit of an adoption row must be a dependency, not a `pub mod`. NEXT STEP: split the domain dependency, then move budget/diversify/ladder/embed, then make darkhold depend on it and delete its copies (adoption proved by deletion), then suki.

open_requirements.requirement: Seed the instance from the operator's rated reading list, through the product's own write path: measure first, prove the write path, then a dry-run seeder, then apply through the service, then rebuild what the ratings feed. The list is a prior, not a population, and the plan says so.
open_requirements.notes: Registered 2026-11-12 because the repository held a dated roadmap that this ledger did not: the idea catalogue's coverage gate refused to regenerate until every idea a live roadmap names had a home, and the honest home for a proposal is a row, not an exemption. Measured basis (taste_census.py, 2026-11-11): accounts 20, taste_profiles 2, instance_theme 1, rating 0, work_ratings 0, work_taste_vectors 0 — twenty accounts and not one rating, so every ranking surface on the busiest member is decoration. Phases: 0 measure, 1 the write path (estate ledger 406, a prerequisite), 2 the seeder with a dry run first, 3 apply through the service, 4 rebuild the taste vectors and the instance theme, 5 the verification that closes it. Non-goal stated in the document: this is one person's list and may not be presented as a population. PLAN RECORDED 2026-11-16, NO CODE IMPLEMENTED: the write path already exists (`PUT /works/{id}/rating` → `reading::upsert_rating`); the blocker is owner data and an owner-gated census, not a missing route. Measured sidecar target: 268 lines, 218 matched, 3 wrapped_title (reported, never guessed), 47 unmatched, 218 distinct ids. Decision: append-only audit sidecar instead of `rating.source` DDL or `taste_provenance`; `is_public=false`; ratings keyed by pseud. Fixed accept rule before apply: ≥180 exact, ≤20 ambiguous, ≥180 applied, and ≥1 overlap with the operator’s top-10 personal recommendations; failure opens a wiring row, never a new ranking crate. Task 0 stop: deploy tree dirty/behind, so no deployed-unit work until those docs paths are committed or set aside. Estate row 407 remains owner-gated.
